newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa given oxygen to help breathing.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa given oxygen to help breathing.

text.p: Doctors said on Tuesday that they gave Mother Teresa oxygen overnight to help her overcome a brief spell of breathing trouble.

"Mother had (a) breathing problem last night around 2.30 a.m. (2100 GMT Monday)," Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre said in an update on the condition of the 86-year-old nun, recovering from heart surgery and pneumonia.
"It lasted for a few minutes and she was put on an oxygen mask," the medical bulletin said. "She is all right now. She had her morning tea around 7.45 a.m. and her prayer."
Last month the Roman Catholic missionary, who was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, had surgery to unblock two coronary arteries, the third such operation in five years.
Her recovery has been complicated by her irregular heartbeat as well as lung and kidney problems.
On Monday, doctors gave her a second mild electric shock in six days to correct her faltering heartbeat. They said the procedure, called cardioversion, was a success.
On Monday evening, the 1979 Nobel peace prize winner walked within the heart clinic's intensive therapy unit, doctors said.

Mother Teresa, who has been pressing doctors to let her go home, called her Missionaries of Charity religious order in the evening and playfully asked the sisters there to send an ambulance to pick her up, doctors said.
Doctors hope she will be well enough to go home for Christmas, but they have warned that her recovery will be slow and that she might never be as active as before.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda was scheduled to pay a short visit to Mother Teresa on Tuesday afternoon during a trip to Calcutta.
"We need lots of prayer to correct her pulmonary infection and we believe our prayers will help her to recover fully," Sister Nirmala of the Missionaries of Charity order told reporters.
